```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(zoo)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(whychusModel)
library(reticulate)

# Ensure Python packages are available in the reticulate managed environment
py_require("pandas")
py_require("numpy")
py_require("requests")

# ── Location ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
LAT      <- 44.390278
LON      <- -121.406792
GRIDPT   <- "PDT/35,57"

# ── Lead days used throughout ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
LEAD_LABELS <- c("0" = "ERA5 / GFS Analysis", "1" = "Day 1", "3" = "Day 3", "7" = "Day 7")
LEAD_COLORS <- c(
  "ERA5 / GFS Analysis" = "darkgreen",
  "Day 1"  = "#E24B4A",
  "Day 3"  = "#888780",
  "Day 7"  = "#378ADD"
)

# ── Shared theme ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
theme_fw <- function(...) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position    = "top",
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(color = "grey40"),
      plot.caption       = element_text(color = "grey60", size = 9),
      ...
    )
}
```

---

# Overview

This document compares three weather forecast data sources used in (or considered for) the RM 8.5 instream temperature forecasting workflow:

| Source | Description | Period | Access |
|--------|-------------|--------|--------|
| **Open-Meteo (GFS Seamless)** | Archived GFS model runs via Open-Meteo Historical Forecast API. Used as inputs to the RF model. | 2019–present | `get_historical_forecast()` |
| **NWS API** | Official NWS gridded forecast for gridpoint PDT/35,57. Currently used for real-time predictions. | Logged May 2026–present | `get_nws_forecast()` |
| **dynamical.org GFS** | Raw GFS forecast and analysis archived via Icechunk/Zarr. Accessed via Python. | May 2021–present | Python `icechunk` + `xarray` |

**Location:** Whychus Creek RM 8.5 — `r LAT`°N, `r LON`°W
**Variables of interest:** Max 2m air temperature, min 2m air temperature, cloud cover

---

# 1. Open-Meteo GFS Seamless — Historical Forecasts

The `all_historical_forecasts` dataset contains archived GFS output from Open-Meteo at lead days 1, 3, and 7, plus ERA5 reanalysis as a baseline observation proxy. This is the training data used in the RF model.

```{r open-meteo-load}
# all_historical_forecasts: valid_date, issue_date, lead_days, variable, value, units, lat, lon, type
hist_fc <- all_historical_forecasts |>
  mutate(
    lead_label = recode(as.character(lead_days), !!!LEAD_LABELS),
    lead_label = factor(lead_label, levels = names(LEAD_COLORS)),
    var_label  = recode(variable,
      "temperature_2m_max" = "Max Air Temp (°C)",
      "temperature_2m_min" = "Min Air Temp (°C)",
      "cloud_cover_mean"   = "Cloud Cover (%)"
    )
  )

hist_fc |>
  group_by(var_label, lead_label) |>
  summarise(
    start     = min(valid_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    end       = max(valid_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    n         = n(),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(value))
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Open-Meteo historical forecast coverage by variable and lead time")
```

## Seasonal mean by lead time

```{r open-meteo-seasonal, fig.height=7}
plot_seasonal <- hist_fc |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(month = month(valid_date, label = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(month, var_label, lead_label) |>
  summarise(mean_value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(plot_seasonal, aes(x = month, y = mean_value, color = lead_label, group = lead_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~var_label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = LEAD_COLORS, name = "Lead time") +
  labs(
    title    = "Open-Meteo GFS Seamless — monthly mean by lead time",
    subtitle = paste0("44.39°N, 121.41°W | ", min(hist_fc$valid_date, na.rm=T), " – ", max(hist_fc$valid_date, na.rm=T)),
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = "Source: Open-Meteo Historical Forecast API (gfs_seamless); ERA5 reanalysis for lead 0"
  ) +
  theme_fw()
```

## Forecast error vs. ERA5 baseline by lead time

Comparing each lead's forecast value against the ERA5 observed value for the same valid date quantifies how much forecast skill degrades with lead time at this location.

```{r open-meteo-bias, fig.height=6}
era5 <- hist_fc |>
  filter(lead_days == 0) |>
  select(valid_date, variable, obs = value)

bias_df <- hist_fc |>
  filter(lead_days > 0) |> 
  inner_join(era5, by = c("valid_date", "variable")) |>
  mutate(error = value - obs)

bias_summary <- bias_df |>
  group_by(var_label, lead_label) |>
  summarise(
    bias = mean(error, na.rm = TRUE),
    mae  = mean(abs(error), na.rm = TRUE),
    rmse = sqrt(mean(error^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    n    = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(bias_summary, digits = 2,
      caption = "Open-Meteo GFS vs. ERA5 — error metrics by variable and lead time")
```

```{r open-meteo-error-dist, eval=FALSE, fig.height=6, include=FALSE}
bias_df |>
  filter(variable %in% c("temperature_2m_max", "temperature_2m_min")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = error, fill = lead_label)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  facet_grid(var_label ~ lead_label, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = LEAD_COLORS, guide = "none") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  labs(
    title   = "Forecast error distribution: GFS vs. ERA5",
    x       = "Error (forecast − ERA5, °C)", y = "Count",
    caption = "Positive = warm bias; negative = cool bias"
  ) +
  theme_fw()
```

# 2. NWS Real-Time Forecast Log

The NWS API (gridpoint PDT/35,57) is pulled daily by `run-daily-forecast.R`. Results are appended to `output/nws-forecasts-log.csv`. This section summarises the logged NWS forecasts and current real-time forecast.

```{r nws-load}
nws_log_path <- here("output", "nws-forecasts-log.csv")

nws_log <- read_csv(nws_log_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    run_date      = as.Date(run_date),
    forecast_date = as.Date(forecast_date),
    lead_days     = as.integer(lead_days)
  )

cat(sprintf("NWS log: %d rows | %s to %s\n",
    nrow(nws_log), min(nws_log$run_date), max(nws_log$run_date)))
```

```{r nws-current}
# Pull live NWS forecast — gracefully fall back to log if API is unavailable
nws_live <- tryCatch({
  bind_rows(
    get_nws_forecast(GRIDPT, "maxTemperature") |> mutate(source = "NWS live"),
    get_nws_forecast(GRIDPT, "minTemperature") |> mutate(source = "NWS live"),
    get_nws_forecast(GRIDPT, "skyCover")       |> mutate(source = "NWS live")
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  message("NWS API unavailable: ", e$message)
  NULL
})

if (!is.null(nws_live)) {
  cat(sprintf("Live NWS pull successful — %d rows, variables: %s\n",
      nrow(nws_live), paste(unique(nws_live$variable), collapse = ", ")))
} else {
  cat("Using forecast log for NWS comparison.\n")
}
```

## Logged NWS forecasts — daily max & min temperature

```{r nws-log-plot, fig.height=5}
nws_daily <- nws_log |>
  filter(variable %in% c("maxTemperature", "minTemperature")) |>
  group_by(run_date, forecast_date, lead_days, variable) |>
  summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    var_label  = recode(variable,
      "maxTemperature" = "Max Air Temp (°C)",
      "minTemperature" = "Min Air Temp (°C)"
    ),
    lead_label = case_when(
      lead_days == 0 ~ "Same day",
      lead_days == 1 ~ "Day 1",
      lead_days == 3 ~ "Day 3",
      lead_days == 7 ~ "Day 7",
      TRUE           ~ paste0("Day ", lead_days)
    )
  )

# Summarise to one value per forecast_date × lead × variable (mean across run dates)
nws_fc_summary <- nws_daily |>
  group_by(forecast_date, lead_days, lead_label, var_label) |>
  summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(lead_days %in% c(0, 1, 3, 7))

ggplot(nws_fc_summary, aes(x = forecast_date, y = value,
                            color = lead_label, group = lead_label)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~var_label, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "Lead") +
  labs(
    title    = "NWS API daily forecasts — logged runs",
    subtitle = paste0("Gridpoint ", GRIDPT, " | ", min(nws_daily$run_date), " – ", max(nws_daily$run_date)),
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = "Source: api.weather.gov"
  ) +
  theme_fw()
```

# 3. dynamical.org GFS — Python Access

dynamical.org archives the raw NOAA GFS model output in Icechunk/Zarr format on AWS S3. Two datasets are relevant:

- **GFS Forecast** (`noaa-gfs-forecast`): initialized every 6 h, 0–384 h lead, from 2021-05-01 onward
- **GFS Analysis** (`noaa-gfs-analysis`): analysis-time GFS fields (no lead time), 2021-05-01 onward

Both datasets include `temperature_2m`, `maximum_temperature_2m`, `minimum_temperature_2m`, and `total_cloud_cover_atmosphere` at 0.25° resolution.

> **Zarr store:** `s3://dynamical-noaa-gfs/noaa-gfs-forecast/v0.2.7.icechunk/`

```{python dyn-setup}
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

# Try dynamical package first, fall back to icechunk + xarray
DYN_AVAILABLE = False
ICE_AVAILABLE = False

try:
    import dynamical
    DYN_AVAILABLE = True
    print("dynamical package available")
except ImportError:
    print("dynamical not found — trying icechunk + xarray")

try:
    import icechunk
    import xarray as xr
    ICE_AVAILABLE = True
    print("icechunk + xarray available")
except ImportError:
    print("icechunk not available")

print(f"DYN_AVAILABLE={DYN_AVAILABLE}, ICE_AVAILABLE={ICE_AVAILABLE}")
```

```{python dyn-fetch-forecast}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Target location
LAT = 44.390278
LON = -121.406792  # xarray typically wants 0-360; GFS uses -180 to 180

dyn_fcst_df  = pd.DataFrame()
dyn_anal_df  = pd.DataFrame()

def open_gfs_forecast():
    """Open GFS forecast via dynamical or icechunk, return xarray Dataset."""
    if DYN_AVAILABLE:
        return dynamical.open_dataset("noaa-gfs-forecast")
    elif ICE_AVAILABLE:
        storage = icechunk.StorageConfig.s3_anonymous(
            bucket="dynamical-noaa-gfs",
            prefix="noaa-gfs-forecast/v0.2.7.icechunk/",
            region="us-east-1"
        )
        repo = icechunk.Repository.open(storage=storage)
        return xr.open_zarr(repo.readonly_session(), consolidated=False)
    else:
        return None

def open_gfs_analysis():
    """Open GFS analysis via dynamical or icechunk, return xarray Dataset."""
    if DYN_AVAILABLE:
        return dynamical.open_dataset("noaa-gfs-analysis")
    elif ICE_AVAILABLE:
        # Fetch analysis STAC URL for the correct version
        import requests
        stac = requests.get(
            "https://stac.dynamical.org/noaa-gfs-analysis/collection.json",
            timeout=10
        ).json()
        href = stac["assets"]["zarr"]["href"]
        storage = icechunk.StorageConfig.s3_anonymous(
            bucket=href.split("/")[2],
            prefix="/".join(href.split("/")[3:]),
            region="us-east-1"
        )
        repo = icechunk.Repository.open(storage=storage)
        return xr.open_zarr(repo.readonly_session(), consolidated=False)
    else:
        return None

# ── GFS Forecast ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if DYN_AVAILABLE or ICE_AVAILABLE:
    try:
        import xarray as xr
        ds_fcst = open_gfs_forecast()

        if ds_fcst is not None:
            print("GFS Forecast dataset opened")
            print("Variables:", list(ds_fcst.data_vars)[:8])

            # Pull the most recent 60 days of 00Z init runs at lead 1d, 3d, 7d
            # init_time dimension, lead_time dimension
            today_utc = pd.Timestamp.now(tz="UTC").floor("D")
            start_init = today_utc - pd.Timedelta(days=60)

            # Slice to our window and nearest point
            point = ds_fcst.sel(
                latitude=LAT, longitude=LON, method="nearest"
            )

            # Subset init times
            init_times = pd.date_range(start=start_init, end=today_utc, freq="D")
            init_times_avail = [t for t in init_times
                                if t in point.init_time.values]

            rows = []
            vars_want = {
                "maximum_temperature_2m" : "temperature_2m_max",
                "minimum_temperature_2m" : "temperature_2m_min",
                "total_cloud_cover_atmosphere": "cloud_cover_mean"
            }
            for lead_days in [1, 3, 7]:
                lt = pd.Timedelta(days=lead_days)
                for it in init_times_avail[:30]:  # limit to 30 init times for speed
                    try:
                        snap = point.sel(init_time=it, lead_time=lt, method="nearest")
                        valid_dt = it + lt
                        for raw_var, clean_var in vars_want.items():
                            if raw_var in snap:
                                val = float(snap[raw_var].values)
                                # Convert K → °C for temperature
                                if "temperature" in raw_var and val > 100:
                                    val -= 273.15
                                rows.append({
                                    "source"    : "dynamical_gfs_forecast",
                                    "init_date" : it.date(),
                                    "valid_date": valid_dt.date(),
                                    "lead_days" : lead_days,
                                    "variable"  : clean_var,
                                    "value"     : round(val, 3)
                                })
                    except Exception:
                        pass

            dyn_fcst_df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
            print(f"GFS Forecast: {len(dyn_fcst_df)} rows")
        else:
            print("GFS Forecast dataset is None")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"GFS Forecast fetch failed: {e}")
else:
    print("No Python data access packages available — skipping dynamical.org pull")
    print("Install with: pip install dynamical  OR  pip install icechunk xarray")
```

```{python dyn-fetch-analysis}
# ── GFS Analysis ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if DYN_AVAILABLE or ICE_AVAILABLE:
    try:
        import xarray as xr
        ds_anal = open_gfs_analysis()

        if ds_anal is not None:
            print("GFS Analysis dataset opened")

            today_utc = pd.Timestamp.now(tz="UTC").floor("D")
            start_anal = today_utc - pd.Timedelta(days=60)

            point_anal = ds_anal.sel(
                latitude=LAT, longitude=LON, method="nearest"
            )

            # time dimension (not init_time × lead_time)
            time_slice = point_anal.sel(time=slice(start_anal, today_utc))

            rows_a = []
            vars_want = {
                "maximum_temperature_2m" : "temperature_2m_max",
                "minimum_temperature_2m" : "temperature_2m_min",
                "total_cloud_cover_atmosphere": "cloud_cover_mean"
            }
            # Resample to daily
            for raw_var, clean_var in vars_want.items():
                if raw_var not in time_slice:
                    continue
                agg = "max" if "maximum" in raw_var else (
                      "min" if "minimum" in raw_var else "mean")
                daily = getattr(time_slice[raw_var].resample(time="1D"), agg)()
                vals = daily.compute().values.tolist()
                dates = [pd.Timestamp(t).date() for t in daily.time.values]
                for d, v in zip(dates, vals):
                    if v is not None and not np.isnan(v):
                        fval = float(v)
                        if "temperature" in raw_var and fval > 100:
                            fval -= 273.15
                        rows_a.append({
                            "source"    : "dynamical_gfs_analysis",
                            "valid_date": d,
                            "variable"  : clean_var,
                            "value"     : round(fval, 3)
                        })

            dyn_anal_df = pd.DataFrame(rows_a)
            print(f"GFS Analysis: {len(dyn_anal_df)} rows")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"GFS Analysis fetch failed: {e}")
```

```{r dyn-to-r}
# Pull Python DataFrames into R
dyn_fcst <- tryCatch(py$dyn_fcst_df, error = function(e) NULL)
dyn_anal <- tryCatch(py$dyn_anal_df, error = function(e) NULL)

# Convert to tibble and fix types
clean_dyn_df <- function(df) {
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(NULL)
  df |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(across(any_of(c("valid_date", "init_date")), as.Date))
}

dyn_fcst <- clean_dyn_df(dyn_fcst)
dyn_anal <- clean_dyn_df(dyn_anal)

cat(sprintf("dynamical.org GFS Forecast: %d rows\n", if (is.null(dyn_fcst)) 0L else nrow(dyn_fcst)))
cat(sprintf("dynamical.org GFS Analysis: %d rows\n", if (is.null(dyn_anal)) 0L else nrow(dyn_anal)))

# If Python packages unavailable, note it
if (is.null(dyn_fcst)) {
  cat("\nNote: dynamical.org data could not be fetched.\n")
  cat("Install Python packages to enable this section:\n")
  cat("  pip install dynamical\n")
  cat("  OR\n")
  cat("  pip install icechunk xarray\n")
}
```

# 4. Cross-Source Comparison

## 4a. NWS vs. dynamical.org GFS — overlapping period

The NWS API returns the official forecast with MOS post-processing and human adjustments. The dynamical.org GFS forecast is raw model output. Both should be similar for the same valid date and lead, but differences reflect NWS post-processing.

```{r nws-vs-dyn, fig.height=7}
if (!is.null(dyn_fcst) && nrow(dyn_fcst) > 0) {

  # Standardise NWS log to same schema
  nws_std <- nws_log |>
    filter(variable %in% c("maxTemperature", "minTemperature")) |>
    group_by(run_date, forecast_date, lead_days, variable) |>
    summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(
      variable  = recode(variable,
        "maxTemperature" = "temperature_2m_max",
        "minTemperature" = "temperature_2m_min"
      ),
      source = "NWS API (weather.gov)"
    ) |>
    rename(valid_date = forecast_date, init_date = run_date)

  # Standardise dynamical GFS forecast
  dyn_std <- dyn_fcst |>
    filter(variable %in% c("temperature_2m_max", "temperature_2m_min")) |>
    mutate(source = "dynamical.org GFS forecast") |>
    rename(init_date = init_date)

  combined <- bind_rows(nws_std, dyn_std) |>
    filter(lead_days %in% c(1, 3, 7)) |>
    mutate(
      var_label  = recode(variable,
        "temperature_2m_max" = "Max Air Temp (°C)",
        "temperature_2m_min" = "Min Air Temp (°C)"
      ),
      lead_label = paste("Day", lead_days)
    )

  # Need one value per source × valid_date × lead × variable
  combined_daily <- combined |>
    group_by(source, valid_date, lead_days, lead_label, var_label) |>
    summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  ggplot(combined_daily,
         aes(x = valid_date, y = value, color = source, group = source)) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.8, linewidth = 0.8) +
    facet_grid(var_label ~ lead_label, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("NWS API (weather.gov)"       = "#C93312",
                 "dynamical.org GFS forecast"  = "#378ADD"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    labs(
      title    = "NWS API vs. dynamical.org GFS — temperature forecast comparison",
      subtitle = paste0("Lead = 1, 3, 7 days | Overlapping period"),
      x = NULL, y = NULL,
      caption  = "NWS = GFS + MOS post-processing; dynamical.org = raw GFS output"
    ) +
    theme_fw()

} else {
  cat("dynamical.org data unavailable — NWS vs. GFS comparison skipped.\n")

  # Still show NWS log summary across run dates
  nws_log |>
    filter(variable %in% c("maxTemperature", "minTemperature"),
           lead_days %in% c(1, 3, 7)) |>
    group_by(forecast_date, lead_days, variable) |>
    summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(
      var_label  = recode(variable,
        "maxTemperature" = "Max Air Temp (°C)",
        "minTemperature" = "Min Air Temp (°C)"
      ),
      lead_label = paste("Day", lead_days)
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = forecast_date, y = value, color = lead_label)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    facet_grid(var_label ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Lead") +
    labs(
      title    = "NWS API forecast log — logged runs",
      subtitle = paste0("Gridpoint ", GRIDPT),
      x = NULL, y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_fw()
}
```

## 4b. NWS vs. dynamical.org — difference scatter plot

```{r nws-dyn-scatter, fig.height=5}
if (!is.null(dyn_fcst) && nrow(dyn_fcst) > 0) {

  nws_daily_tmax <- nws_log |>
    filter(variable == "maxTemperature") |>
    group_by(forecast_date, lead_days) |>
    summarise(nws_tmax = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  dyn_daily_tmax <- dyn_fcst |>
    filter(variable == "temperature_2m_max") |>
    group_by(valid_date, lead_days) |>
    summarise(dyn_tmax = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  joined <- inner_join(
    nws_daily_tmax |> rename(valid_date = forecast_date),
    dyn_daily_tmax,
    by = c("valid_date", "lead_days")
  ) |>
    filter(lead_days %in% c(1, 3, 7)) |>
    mutate(lead_label = paste("Day", lead_days))

  if (nrow(joined) > 3) {
    ggplot(joined, aes(x = dyn_tmax, y = nws_tmax, color = lead_label)) +
      geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
      geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +
      facet_wrap(~lead_label) +
      scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2", guide = "none") +
      labs(
        title   = "NWS vs. dynamical.org GFS — max temperature scatter",
        x       = "dynamical.org GFS Tmax (°C)",
        y       = "NWS API Tmax (°C)",
        caption = "Dashed line = 1:1; points above line = NWS warmer than raw GFS"
      ) +
      theme_fw()
  } else {
    cat("Insufficient overlapping data for scatter plot.\n")
  }

} else {
  cat("dynamical.org data unavailable — scatter plot skipped.\n")
}
```

## 4c. Open-Meteo GFS vs. dynamical.org GFS — model alignment

Open-Meteo (`gfs_seamless`) and dynamical.org both archive GFS output but with different processing pipelines. For the overlapping period (May 2021 onward), we expect similar but not identical values due to spatial downscaling differences.

```{r openmeteo-vs-dyn, fig.height=7}
if (!is.null(dyn_fcst) && nrow(dyn_fcst) > 0) {

  # Open-Meteo historical at lead 1, 3, 7 — post-2021
  om_recent <- hist_fc |>
    filter(lead_days %in% c(1, 3, 7),
           valid_date >= as.Date("2021-05-01"),
           variable %in% c("temperature_2m_max", "temperature_2m_min", "cloud_cover_mean")) |>
    mutate(source = "Open-Meteo GFS seamless") |>
    select(source, valid_date, lead_days, variable, value)

  dyn_std2 <- dyn_fcst |>
    filter(variable %in% c("temperature_2m_max", "temperature_2m_min", "cloud_cover_mean")) |>
    mutate(source = "dynamical.org GFS forecast") |>
    select(source, valid_date, lead_days, variable, value)

  both <- bind_rows(om_recent, dyn_std2) |>
    filter(lead_days %in% c(1, 3, 7)) |>
    mutate(
      var_label  = recode(variable,
        "temperature_2m_max" = "Max Air Temp (°C)",
        "temperature_2m_min" = "Min Air Temp (°C)",
        "cloud_cover_mean"   = "Cloud Cover (%)"
      ),
      lead_label = paste("Day", lead_days)
    ) |>
    group_by(source, valid_date, lead_days, lead_label, var_label) |>
    summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  ggplot(both, aes(x = valid_date, y = value, color = source)) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_grid(var_label ~ lead_label, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("Open-Meteo GFS seamless"     = "#888780",
                 "dynamical.org GFS forecast"  = "#378ADD"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    labs(
      title    = "Open-Meteo GFS seamless vs. dynamical.org GFS — model alignment",
      subtitle = "Same underlying model, different processing pipelines",
      x = NULL, y = NULL,
      caption  = "Differences reflect spatial downscaling and potential ECMWF blending in Open-Meteo seamless"
    ) +
    theme_fw()

} else {
  cat("dynamical.org data unavailable — Open-Meteo vs. dynamical.org comparison skipped.\n")

  # Show Open-Meteo alone for the recent period
  hist_fc |>
    filter(lead_days %in% c(1, 3, 7),
           valid_date >= as.Date("2021-05-01"),
           variable %in% c("temperature_2m_max", "temperature_2m_min")) |>
    mutate(month = month(valid_date, label = TRUE)) |>
    group_by(month, var_label, lead_label) |>
    summarise(mean_value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |> invisible()

  # fallback plot if dyn not available - already shown above, skip
  cat("Open-Meteo data shown in Section 1.\n")
}
```

# 5. Forecast Skill by Lead Time

Across sources, forecast skill for air temperature degrades with increasing lead time. This section quantifies that degradation for the Open-Meteo archive (largest historical record).

```{r skill-table}
skill <- bias_df |>
  group_by(var_label, lead_days) |>
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    bias     = round(mean(error, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    mae      = round(mean(abs(error), na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    rmse     = round(sqrt(mean(error^2, na.rm = TRUE)), 2),
    r        = tryCatch(round(cor(value, obs, use = "complete.obs"), 3), error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

kable(skill, caption = "GFS forecast skill vs. ERA5 baseline by lead time (Open-Meteo archive)",
      col.names = c("Variable", "Lead (days)", "N", "Bias (°C)", "MAE (°C)", "RMSE (°C)", "r"))
```

```{r skill-plot, fig.height=5}
skill_temp <- skill |> filter(grepl("Temp", var_label))
if (nrow(skill_temp) > 0) {
  skill_temp |>
    pivot_longer(c(bias, mae, rmse), names_to = "metric", values_to = "val") |>
    mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = c("bias", "mae", "rmse"),
                            labels = c("Bias", "MAE", "RMSE"))) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = lead_days, y = val, color = var_label, group = var_label)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 3, 7)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("#C93312", "#378ADD"), name = NULL) +
    labs(
      title   = "Forecast error metrics by lead time",
      x       = "Lead time (days)", y = NULL,
      caption = "Source: Open-Meteo Historical Forecast API vs. ERA5 reanalysis"
    ) +
    theme_fw()
} else {
  cat("No ERA5 baseline available — forecast skill plot skipped.\n")
}
```

# 6. Source Summary and Recommendations

```{r summary-table, echo=FALSE}
summary_tbl <- tribble(
  ~Source,              ~`Data type`,     ~`Temporal coverage`,  ~`Lead times`,     ~`Resolution`, ~`Access`,         ~`Notes`,
  "Open-Meteo GFS seamless", "Historical archive", "2019–present",  "1, 3, 7 d",       "~25 km",      "R: `get_historical_forecast()`", "ERA5 baseline pre-2019; blends ECMWF at longer leads",
  "NWS API (weather.gov)", "Real-time forecast",  "Logged May 2026+", "0–7+ d",        "~2.5 km",     "R: `get_nws_forecast()`",       "MOS post-processing; human adjustments",
  "dynamical.org GFS forecast", "Real-time + archive", "May 2021–present", "0–384 h", "~25 km",      "Python: `dynamical` or `icechunk+xarray`", "Raw GFS; hourly → 3-hourly",
  "dynamical.org GFS analysis", "Analysis (no lead)",  "May 2021–present", "n/a",     "~25 km",      "Python: `dynamical` or `icechunk+xarray`", "Best available GFS-grid observation proxy"
)

kable(summary_tbl, caption = "Weather forecast source comparison")
```

**Key differences between sources:**

- **NWS vs. raw GFS:** NWS applies MOS bias correction and human edits, particularly for temperature. Expect NWS to be 1–3°C warmer/cooler than raw GFS on any given day. For real-time forecasting, NWS is operationally tested and locally calibrated — preferred for the current RF model.

- **Open-Meteo vs. dynamical.org GFS:** Both derive from GFS but Open-Meteo applies statistical downscaling and blends ECMWF at lead > ~5 days. Dynamical.org is closer to the raw GFS grid output. The Open-Meteo archive is suitable for model training; dynamical.org's analysis product provides a useful cross-check.

- **Temporal depth:** For training the RF model, Open-Meteo (2019–present) provides the longest GFS-archive record. ERA5 extends coverage to 2011 at the cost of swapping from a forecast to a reanalysis product.

**Recommendation for RM 8.5 model:**
- Continue using `get_nws_forecast()` (NWS API) for real-time predictions — it is operationally reliable and already integrated.
- Use Open-Meteo GFS seamless (`get_historical_forecast()`) for training data — longest consistent archive.
- Use dynamical.org GFS analysis as a secondary validation benchmark for recent years (2021–present) where both sources overlap.
